record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Show that if condition (G) fails, or if there is a hidden infinity, in a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition, then the spacetime contains a trapped surface; thereby prove that such a cosmological spacetime is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R x M and is static.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{n+1}, g)$ be a cosmological spacetime, that is, a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold admitting a compact Cauchy hypersurface. Assume that $(M,g)$ satisfies the timelike convergence condition, $\mathrm{Ric}(X,X) \ge 0$ for every timelike vector $X$.

Recall the following notions:
- (Condition G) Every inextendible timelike geodesic in $(M,g)$ has both past and future endpoints on the "cosmological boundary" in the sense that no incomplete timelike geodesic ray escapes to a "hidden" portion of the spacetime; equivalently, the spacetime contains no timelike line confined to a region invisible from any Cauchy surface (a "hidden infinity").
- A hidden infinity is a region of $(M,g)$ where future or past inextendible causal geodesics fail to be captured by the family of Cauchy surfaces, allowing observers/geodesics to "escape" without completing.
- A trapped surface is a compact spacelike codimension-2 submanifold $\Sigma \subset M$ whose two future-directed null mean curvature vectors are both past-directed timelike (i.e., both null expansions are negative).

Prove the following:

(a) If condition (G) fails, or if $(M,g)$ contains a hidden infinity, then $(M,g)$ contains a trapped surface.

(b) Consequently, any cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete, or it splits isometrically as a metric product $(\mathbb{R} \times N, -dt^2 \oplus h)$ for some compact Riemannian manifold $(N,h)$ and is static.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is connected to Bartnik's splitting conjecture for cosmological spacetimes, which remains a major open problem in mathematical relativity. Recent works (e.g., Galloway–Ling on CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting, 2019; Ling on omniscient foliations, 2022; examples without CMC foliations, 2023) make partial progress but do not resolve the conjecture in full. No source verifies the specific implication "(G) fails or hidden infinity ⇒ trapped surface" in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Globally hyperbolic spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces satisfying the strong energy condition: if timelike geodesically complete, then splits as a product.
status_evidence.claim: Bartnik's splitting conjecture remains an open problem with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Omniscient foliations and the geometry of cosmological spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric conditions on foliations impede null geodesic lines in cosmological spacetimes; partial restrictions toward Bartnik's splitting conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress, conjecture still open.

status_evidence.title: Examples of cosmological spacetimes without CMC Cauchy surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs cosmological spacetimes lacking CMC foliations, showing limits of approaches to the splitting conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The full conjecture and related trapped-surface implications remain unresolved.
